product.name: 10-Day Adelaide to Perth Adventure Tour
product.shortDescription: Cross Australia from Adelaide to Perth on the swag camping adventure. Hike rugged landscapes, swim at world class beaches, meet iconic wildlife and sleep beneath star filled skies on an unforgettable journey through the heart of Australia.
product.description:
UNTAMED MOMENTS

  • Cross the vast Nullarbor Plain with endless horizons, red dirt roads and classic Aussie roadhouse stops.
  • Swim, surf and soak up some of Australia’s most ridiculously beautiful coastlines.
  • Stand high above the crashing Southern Ocean at the epic Bunda Cliffs.
  • Hike through rugged national parks packed with granite peaks, wild bushland and coastal views.
  • Learn to surf, carve down giant sand dunes and embrace your inner wildling.
  • Chill with the kangaroos on the snow white sands of Lucky Bay.
  • Roll up your sleeves and give back during a hands on wildlife conservation experience.
  • Step inside ancient Ngilgi Cave for a powerful cultural experience connecting to Country.
  • Sip, snack and taste your way through the legendary Margaret River region.
  • Swim alongside playful sea lions and dolphins in one seriously unforgettable marine encounter (OE).

INCLUSIONS

  • Meals – 9 breakfasts, 3 lunches, 8 dinners
  • Accommodation – Swag camping with basic facilities (8 nights) and bush camp with no facilities (1 night)
  • All National Park and entry fees
  • All activities, unless stated as an optional extra (OE)
  • Transport – Air-conditioned coaster bus (max 20 people)

 

ITINERARY

Day 1 | Adelaide to Mount Remarkable National Park


We leave Adelaide early and begin our coast to coast adventure, travelling north through regional South Australia towards the Yorke Peninsula.

Our first stop is Wallaroo, where there is time to stretch the legs and grab a coffee before continuing through coastal towns to Port Germein, home to one of Australia’s longest timber jetties.

By late afternoon, we arrive at Mount Remarkable National Park, a hidden gem in the Southern Flinders Ranges. Rugged peaks, ancient river red gums and abundant wildlife make this a spectacular introduction to outback South Australia.
One of those places that quietly exceeds every expectation.

After setting up camp at Mambray Creek, we head out on a short bushwalk to experience the park before gathering around our first camp dinner together.

As the sun sets, the group begins to settle into life on the road, sharing stories before rolling out our swags beneath a sky filled with stars.

Accommodation: Swag camping with amenities at Mambray Creek Campground

Meals Included: Dinner

Distance Travelled: Approx. 320 km


Day 2 | Mount Remarkable to the Eyre Peninsula


We wake to the sounds of the bush before setting out on the Davey’s Gully Hike, an easy morning walk through native bushland with sweeping views across Spencer Gulf and the surrounding ranges.

From here, we continue west to the Eyre Peninsula, stopping in Kimba, a welcoming outback town known for its giant silo artwork and strong community spirit. We visit Workshop26, a former tractor shed transformed into a creative community space showcasing local art, handmade products and stories from the people who call this region home.

Lunch is prepared by volunteers from the Kimba Hospital Auxiliary and Royal Flying Doctor Service support crew, with every meal helping support vital services in remote South Australia.
" A simple lunch that directly supports the local community." 

As we reach the Eyre Peninsula, rolling farmland gives way to towering sand dunes, rugged coastline and fresh ocean air.

By late afternoon, we arrive at Coodlie Park Farm Retreat, an off grid eco camp built by Untamed Escapes founders Craig and Cathy. Tonight, we settle in for dinner before those interested can join an optional stargazing experience beneath some of Australia’s darkest skies.
This is where the outback begins to slow you down.

Accommodation: Swag camping with amenities at Coodlie Park Farm Retreat 

Meals Included: Breakfast, Lunch, Dinner

Distance Travelled: Approx. 450 km


Day 3 | Baird Bay to Penong


We start early for one of the most memorable experiences of the trip, the optional Baird Bay sea lion and dolphin swim.

Heading out by boat, we have the chance to swim with wild Australian sea lions and bottlenose dolphins in their natural environment. Curious sea lions often dart and play around the group while dolphins cruise through the bay nearby. There is no feeding or staged interaction, just genuine wildlife encounters on their terms.
" Usually the moment people are still talking about long after the trip ends."

For those not joining the swim, the morning is free to relax around Baird Bay before we meet up again for lunch.

In the afternoon, we head to Streaky Bay Surf School for a two hour surf lesson. Whether it is your first time on a board or you are looking to improve your skills, local instructors will have you riding waves in one of South Australia’s most beautiful surf locations. If surfing is not for you, there is time to relax on the beach or enjoy the coastline instead.

" Not a bad place to spend an afternoon on the Eyre Peninsula."

By evening, we arrive in Penong, where we settle into camp, share dinner and swap stories from another incredible day on the coast.

Accommodation: Swag camping with amenities at Penong Caravan Park
Meals Included: Breakfast, Lunch
Distance Travelled: Approx. 400 km

 

Day 4 | Nullarbor Plain


Today, we begin one of Australia’s great road trips, crossing the vast Nullarbor Plain. Long straight roads, endless horizons and wide open skies make the journey as memorable as the destinations themselves.

Along the way, we stop for photos at the famous outback road signs before reaching the spectacular Bunda Cliffs, where the limestone plateau drops dramatically into the Southern Ocean. Standing on the edge, with waves crashing far below, is a reminder of just how vast and wild this coastline really is.
"One of the most dramatic coastal views anywhere in Australia."

After a stop at the iconic Nullarbor Roadhouse, we cross into Western Australia and continue to our most remote camp of the trip.

Tonight, we experience authentic outback bush camping beneath some of the darkest skies in the world. With no reception, no crowds and nothing but the sounds of nature, it is a night many travellers never forget.

Accommodation: Bush camping on the Nullarbor (no facilities)
Meals Included: Breakfast, Dinner
Distance Travelled: Approx. 600 km

 

Day 5 | Nullarbor to Cape Le Grand National Park


This morning, we continue west along the famous 90 Mile Straight, the longest straight stretch of road in Australia.

The drive itself becomes part of the experience out here. Roadhouses appear out of nowhere, old stories from the Nullarbor come to life through the guide, and the landscapes slowly begin to shift once again.

We stop through Balladonia and Norseman before the red dirt finally gives way to bright white beaches and impossibly blue water as we approach Esperance.

By afternoon, we arrive at Cape Le Grand National Park, one of the most beautiful coastal regions in Australia. 

“ Kangaroos on white sand, turquoise water and empty beaches, this is the side of Australia most travellers dream about.” 

We set up camp at Lucky Bay, our home for the next two nights. 

Distance travelled: Approximately 800 km

Accommodation: Swag camping with amenities at Lucky Bay Campground 

Meals included: Breakfast, Dinner

 

Day 6 | Cape Le Grand National Park


Today is all about slowing down and properly experiencing Cape Le Grand.

Those keen for a challenge can take on the hike up Frenchman Peak, a steep climb across granite slabs with huge views waiting at the top. Looking out across the Recherche Archipelago from the summit is one of the best rewards of the trip.

The rest of the day is left open to enjoy the national park properly. Some people spend hours swimming in the bays, others head off on walking trails or simply relax on the sand with nowhere else to be.

Cape Le Grand has a way of making people slow down. The beaches are unbelievably white, the water shifts between deep blue and turquoise, and even the kangaroos seem more relaxed here.

“ Most people could easily spend a week here and still not want to leave.” 

There are no long drives today, no schedules to rush through and no shortage of incredible places to stop along the coast.

As the sun drops, we return to camp for another relaxed evening at Lucky Bay.

Accommodation: Swag camping at Lucky Bay

Meals included: Breakfast, Lunch, Dinner

Distance travelled: Just 10 minutes around the park


Day 7 | Cape Le Grand National Park to Stirling Ranges


We pack up camp and leave Esperance behind, stopping at Twilight Cove for one final swim or walk along the coast before turning inland.

The drive today takes us through changing landscapes, from open farmland to rugged mountain country, with a stop in Ravensthorpe along the way.

By late afternoon, we arrive in the Stirling Ranges, where sharp peaks rise straight from the bushland around us.

Tonight, we stay at a quiet private campground near Mt Trio. After a few big days on the coast, the change in scenery feels completely different again.
“ One of the best parts of this trip is how quickly the landscapes change from one day to the next.” 

Accommodation: Swag camping with amenities at Mt Trio in the Stirling Ranges 

Meals included: Breakfast, Dinner

Distance travelled: Approximately 500 km


Day 8 | Stirling Ranges & South West Coast


After breakfast, we head into the Porongurups for the hike to Castle Rock and the Granite Skywalk. The trail winds through towering forest before opening onto sweeping views across the surrounding ranges. For those brave enough, the suspended skywalk offers an unforgettable perspective.

From here, we continue to the coast and visit The Gap and Natural Bridge near Albany, where the powerful Southern Ocean crashes against the rugged granite cliffs.

Later, we make our way to Greens Pool and Elephant Rocks, two of Western Australia’s most beautiful beaches and the perfect place for a swim when conditions allow.
" This is the stretch of coastline that often surprises people the most."

Towards evening, we enter the forests of the Walpole region to visit the famous Giant Tingle Tree, an ancient giant that has stood here for centuries.

Tonight, we settle into camp at Quinninup, surrounded by towering karri forest and another peaceful night beneath the trees.

Accommodation: Swag camping with amenities at Quinninup Eco Tourist Park

Meals included: Breakfast, Dinner

Distance travelled: Around 390 km

 

Day 9 | Quinninup to Margaret River


This morning, we visit the Capes Raptor Centre, one of Australia’s leading bird of prey rehabilitation centres. Going behind the scenes, we help support the care of injured and displaced raptors while learning more about eagles, hawks, owls and falcons from the passionate team caring for them.
"A hands on conservation experience that leaves a lasting impression."

Later, we arrive in Margaret River, with free time to explore the town, enjoy lunch or browse its local galleries and boutique shops.

The afternoon is dedicated to discovering the region’s renowned food and wine scene, with visits to a selection of local producers. Depending on the day, we may stop at wineries, distilleries, chocolate makers or artisan cheese producers, each showcasing the flavours that make Margaret River famous.

By evening, we arrive at our campsite in the Margaret River region. Campsites vary depending on the season, but each offers a peaceful setting to relax with the group and enjoy one final night camping in Western Australia’s southwest.

Accommodation: Swag camping with amenities at Fair Harvest Permaculture Farm (or RAC Margaret River Nature Park)

Meals included: Breakfast, Dinner

Distance travelled: Around 240 km

 

Day 10 | Margaret River to Perth


We roll up the swags one last time before joining Wadandi custodian Josh “Koomal” Whiteland for a cultural experience through Country.

The morning includes bushwalking, stories of the six Noongar seasons, bush foods, native medicine and traditional fire lighting, before continuing underground into Ngilgi Cave. Hearing the didgeridoo echo through the cave is one of the quieter moments of the trip, but also one of the most memorable.
A powerful way to finish the journey across Western Australia.

Later, we stop in Busselton, where there is time for a walk along the famous 1.8 km jetty and a final coffee or snack before the drive back to Perth.

By the time we arrive that evening, most people are already swapping favourite moments from the trip and wondering how ten days managed to go so quickly.

Meals included: Breakfast

Distance travelled: Around 340 km

 

KNOW BEFORE YOU BOOK

General Information

  • Tour timing: This tour begins in Adelaide on Day 1 at approximately 6:15 am and concludes in Perth around 6:00 pm on Day 10.
  • Dietary requirements: Please let us know about any dietary needs when booking. We cater for most preferences and aim to provide fresh, varied meals. Snacks, soft drinks, and alcohol are not included
  • Luggage limits: Each guest is allowed one soft travel bag or backpack (max 15 kg) plus a small daypack or piece of hand luggage. If you are travelling with additional luggage, please contact us directly in advance, as extra luggage fees may apply.
  • Minimum numbers: This tour requires a minimum of four travellers to run. If we need to cancel due to low numbers, we'll offer a transfer to a future date or a full refund.
  • Before you book: Please read our full Booking Terms & Conditions to ensure this experience is right for you.


Accommodation & Camping 

  • This is a participatory camping tour, meaning guests are expected to get involved by helping with basic tasks, such as meal preparation and packing up camp.
  • Accommodation includes a mix of national parks and bush campgrounds. Most campgrounds offer basic toilet and shower facilities, except for the one-night camping on the Nullarbor, where we don't have any amenities.
  • When camping, you'll sleep in a traditional Aussie swag—a sturdy canvas bed roll with a built-in mattress, used under the stars or in wet weather tents.
  • Sleeping bags: Please bring your own sleeping bag and pillow. Alternatively, you can hire a used sleeping bag for $20 during the booking process. All unused or retired sleeping bags are donated to a homeless charity, giving them a second life.
  • Weather conditions: Be prepared for extreme weather, including high temperatures, cold temperatures, and exposure to the elements.
  • In the event of wet weather, group tents will be provided for shared shelter.
  • Should extreme weather affect the camping experience, alternative accommodation may be arranged. Any additional costs will be shared 50/50 between Untamed Escapes and guests.

 

Fitness & Mobility

Our adventure tours are best suited to travellers who love nature, hiking, and spending time outdoors, with a good dose of fun and group camaraderie. To get the most out of your experience, please consider the following:

·       Fitness requirements: A moderate level of fitness is needed. On some days, you may be walking between 3 and 12 km, often on uneven ground and in hot or wet conditions.

·       Mobility considerations: While there's no upper age limit, all travellers should self-assess their mobility and comfort with activities such as hiking, swimming, and swag camping. You'll need to be able to lift yourself from ground level, as swags are traditional ground-based bedding.

 

Itinerary Changes

At Untamed Escapes, your safety and experience are our top priorities. Our guides are trained to adapt plans when needed to ensure a smooth and enjoyable journey. Please keep the following in mind:

  • Experienced guidance: Our storyteller guides continuously assess local conditions such as weather and traffic to deliver the best possible experience.
  • Dynamic weather: The Australian outback is known for sudden and dramatic weather changes. Our team remains informed and responsive to these conditions.
  • Adjustments for safety and comfort:

o   Itinerary changes may occur to improve the overall experience or respond to unexpected circumstances.

o   For example, during the hotter months (December to March), hike times may be adjusted to earlier in the day to avoid high temperatures.

Clear communication: Any itinerary changes will be communicated to the group in advance whenever possible.

extras.name: Swim with Sea Lions & Dolphins at Baird Bay (from Oct 2026)
extras.description:
Operated by the Eco-Accredited Baird Bay Ocean Eco Tours, this is a truly wild and magical marine experience. These animals are never fed or interfered with, ensuring a respectful encounter in their natural habitat. Cruise out to Jones Island, home to a colony of playful Australian sea lions. Slip into the calm waters and snorkel in the shallow rock pools as curious sea lions twirl, dive, and dance around you. Then head into deeper water to swim with wild bottlenose dolphins—graceful, intelligent, and entirely free.

Includes:

- 3-hour boat cruise
- Snorkelling equipment and wetsuits
Tours will be operate from 01 October 2026 until 30 April 2027

extras.name: Plant a Tree With Carbon Positive Australia
extras.description:
We are partnering with Carbon Positive Australia to give you the opportunity to reduce your carbon footprint by planting a tree through their native tree-planting programs across Australia.  

Who Is Carbon Positive Australia?

Carbon Positive Australia helps organisations, communities, and individuals take climate action by
supporting native tree planting and ecosystem restoration. Their reforestation projects are about
more than just carbon offsets - they’re about meaningful restoration, supporting community tree
planting and providing education tools to help everyone understand their climate impact.

Learn more at https://carbonpositiveaustralia.com.au
